make.name: Volvo
make.description: Swedish carmaker founded in 1927 and majority-owned by China's Geely Holding since 2010. Its battery-electric range runs from the EX30 to the EX90 SUV and ES90 sedan, with the EX60 added in 2026. In 2024 Volvo dropped its goal of selling only electric cars by 2030.

models.name: C30 Electric
models.description: Battery-electric version of the C30 hatchback, built in small numbers (around 250 planned) between 2011 and 2012 and leased to fleets and companies, mainly in Sweden and other European countries. It was Volvo's first series-built electric car.

generations.name: Original
generations.description: Converted C30 with a 24 kWh EnerDel lithium-ion pack in the tunnel and fuel-tank space; bodies built in Ghent, motor and battery fitted in Gothenburg. Leased only, never sold outright.

models.name: EX40
models.description: Volvo's first mass-market EV: the battery-electric XC40, revealed in October 2019 and on sale from late 2020 as the XC40 Recharge, renamed EX40 in 2024. It moved from front- to rear-wheel drive for model year 2024. Volvo is dropping it from the US (the 2026 model is the last one there according to most reports) while it stays on sale in Europe.

generations.name: Original (P8 / P6)
generations.description: First battery-electric XC40 on the CMA platform: 78 kWh twin-motor P8 AWD, later joined by a 69 kWh front-drive single motor. The exterior facelift with frameless headlights arrived for model year 2023.

generations.name: Rear-drive update
generations.description: New rear-mounted motors (the first rear-drive Volvo in 25 years), an 82 kWh pack for Extended Range and Twin Motor, and faster DC charging. Renamed EX40 in 2024; Volvo showed a further facelift for model year 2028 in 2026 (not modelled separately yet).

models.name: EC40
models.description: Coupe-roofed, electric-only sibling of the XC40/EX40, revealed in March 2021 as the C40 Recharge and renamed EC40 in 2024. It shares the EX40's powertrains, including the 2023 switch to rear-drive single motors. It is no longer sold in the US but remains on sale in Europe.

generations.name: Original
generations.description: Launch versions on the CMA platform: twin-motor AWD with a 78 kWh pack and a front-drive single motor.

generations.name: Rear-drive update
generations.description: Same rear-drive motors and 82 kWh Extended Range pack as the EX40 update; renamed EC40 in 2024.

models.name: EX30
models.description: Volvo's smallest SUV, built on Geely's SEA platform in China from 2023 and also in Ghent, Belgium and Malaysia from 2025. A raised Cross Country version followed in 2025. Volvo dropped the EX30 from the US after the 2026 model year; it continues in Europe, Canada and other markets.

generations.name: First generation
generations.description: Compact SUV on the SEA platform with a 51 kWh LFP or 69 kWh NMC pack and single- or twin-motor drive.

models.name: EX90
models.description: Seven-seat flagship SUV, revealed in November 2022 as Volvo's first bespoke EV and built in Ridgeville (South Carolina), Chengdu and Malaysia since 2024. For model year 2026 it moved from a 400-volt to an 800-volt system with new motors and faster charging.

generations.name: Original (400 V)
generations.description: SPA2 platform with a 400-volt system, 111 kWh pack for the twin-motor versions and 250 kW DC charging.

generations.name: 800-volt update
generations.description: Moved to an 800-volt electrical system with new 92 kWh and 106 kWh CATL packs, new motors (up to 500 kW in the Twin Motor Performance) and up to 350 kW DC charging.

models.name: ES90
models.description: Large electric liftback sedan revealed in March 2025 on the 800-volt SPA2 platform and built in Chengdu and Malaysia from September 2025. It is sold in Europe and China; Volvo has said it has no current plans to sell it in the US.

generations.name: First generation
generations.description: Executive liftback on SPA2 with an 800-volt system and 92 or 106 kWh CATL packs.

models.name: EM90
models.description: Large luxury electric MPV introduced in November 2023 and built in Ningbo, China, on Geely's SEA platform shared with the Zeekr 009. Sold in China (and selected Asian markets), rear-wheel drive only.

generations.name: First generation
generations.description: Restyled Zeekr 009 with Volvo front and rear ends and a 116 kWh CATL pack.

models.name: EX60
models.description: Mid-size electric SUV revealed on 21 January 2026, the first Volvo on the SPA3 platform, built in Torslanda, Sweden from April 2026. It has an 800-volt system, a native NACS port in North America and is now Volvo's cheapest EV in the US.

generations.name: First generation
generations.description: SPA3 platform, 800-volt system, P6 (RWD), P10 and P12 (AWD) versions; a Cross Country follows for model year 2028.

legacy_notes.note: Legacy 'XC40 Recharge Twin Motor' row (402 hp, 82 kWh, 254 mi) is the MY2024 Twin Motor Performance of the rear-drive update; EPA rates MY2025-26 at 260 mi. Model renamed EX40 in 2024. Legacy price $55,495, 0-60 4.6 s and 112 mph were not re-sourced and are left null. Legacy image (Volvo press photo) shows the facelifted car and is not reused for the original generation.

Legacy row says drive_type AWD: wrong, the Single Motor Extended Range is rear-wheel drive. 293 mi is the MY2024 EPA figure (MY2025-26: 296 mi). Its image (facelifted EX40) is used for the 2024 generation after viewing.

Legacy current_price $34,950 is the never-delivered promised US base price, not a Twin Motor Performance price; the US EX30 went on sale in 2025 at $44,900 (Single Motor Extended Range). Legacy 0-60 3.3 s not re-sourced. EX30 is discontinued in the US after MY2026 (announced March 2026); still sold in Europe/Canada. Legacy image verified as EX30 and reused.
Legacy 'Single Motor LR' = Single Motor Extended Range (69 kWh). Price $36,245 has no source and is dropped; US launch price was $44,900. Discontinued in the US after MY2026.

gaps: WebSearch budget for the session ran out mid-research; remaining facts come from Wikipedia, EPA data and articles already fetched.

EPA lists a 2026 EC40 (298/268 mi) although Electrek (Sept 2026) says the EC40 is no longer sold in the US; US offerings stop at MY2025 and US market status is discontinued.

EX90 original-generation WLTP ranges are inconsistent on Wikipedia; no EU offerings entered. EX90 2026 refresh images: no photo that verifiably shows the 800 V car (exterior unchanged), so none attached.

EX60 P12 US range is Volvo's preliminary 400 mi (is_estimate); EPA had not published it. EX60 P10/P12 UK prices not sourced. EX60 WLTP figures come from Wikipedia without an explicit cycle label (P12 810 km matches the 503-mile WLTP figure reported by Honest John).
EM90 price and ES90 Twin Motor Performance WLTP range not sourced.
Volvo has said a new entry-level EV (reportedly EX50, trademarked July 2026) arrives in the US by end of 2027; not added because the name and specs are not official.
